questions.prompt: You need to replace a RAM module. What must you do first?
choices: Shut down Windows and open the side panel
Shut down, unplug the power cord, then press the power button to drain power
Leave the computer running so you can see when the new RAM works
questions.explanation: The computer must be disconnected from mains power, and remaining standby power drained, before you touch anything inside.

questions.prompt: Where should the anti-static wrist strap be connected?
choices: A painted part of the case
Bare, unpainted metal of the case or the mat's grounding point
questions.explanation: The strap must connect to something conductive and grounded. Paint and plastic do not conduct.

questions.prompt: Which of these are correct ways to handle components? Select all that apply.
choices: Hold modules and cards by their edges
Keep spare parts in anti-static bags until needed
Touch the gold contacts to check they are clean
Put parts down on carpet while you work
Place parts on an anti-static mat
questions.explanation: Avoid touching contacts and never put parts on carpet, which builds up static.

questions.prompt: A customer's power supply is dead. What should you do?
choices: Open it and look for a burnt fuse
Replace the whole power supply unit
Bridge the power switch with a wire
Open it, but only after unplugging it for a minute
questions.explanation: Capacitors in a PSU can hold a dangerous charge even when unplugged. Technicians replace PSUs; they do not open them.

questions.prompt: Put these preparation steps in the correct order.
items: Press and hold the power button for about 5 seconds
Put on the wrist strap and clip it to bare metal
questions.explanation: Remove mains power first, drain what remains, ground yourself, and only then open the case.
